launches.title: Moss: Real-time Semantic Search for Conversational AI
launches.tagline: We help conversational AI teams turn lagging, robotic interactions into natural, human-like experiences through sub-10 ms semantic search.
launches.body:
Hello YC! This is [**Sri Raghu Malireddi**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/r4ghu) from [**Moss**](https://usemoss.dev/).

### **TL;DR**

Moss is a high-performance runtime for real-time semantic search. It delivers sub-10 ms lookups, instant index updates, and zero infra overhead. Moss runs where your agent lives - cloud, in-browser, or on-device - so search feels native and users never wait. You connect your data once; Moss handles indexing, packaging, distribution and updates.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95036&key=user_uploads/2412081/c21db6f6-b453-40b6-a15d-5654971ab2ab)

### **The Problem**

If you’ve ever built a conversational or voice AI product, you’ve felt it - that awkward pause when your agent lags or hesitates. The illusion of conversation breaks, and suddenly it feels less like talking to intelligence and more like waiting for a page to load.

The culprit is almost always retrieval. Every query hops across networks and cloud databases, adding seconds of delay. As usage scales, those small lags snowball into lost users, rising infra and egress costs. Teams spend weeks rebuilding embeddings and indexes, tuning search infra just to get “good enough” answers instead of focusing on what actually matters: building great AI experiences!

### **Solution**

Moss puts real-time semantic search in the same runtime as your agent and application, so you can -

* **Keep retrieval close** - embed & index right alongside your agents (docs, chat history, telemetry).
* **Answer in <10 ms** - local lookups, zero network hops.
* **Manage at scale** - store, sync, and distribute indexes with our managed data layer at [**https://moss.dev**](https://usemoss.dev)
* **Drop-in SDKs** - [**JavaScript**](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@moss-js/moss) and [**Python**](https://pypi.org/project/moss/).

### **Our Story**

Moss founding team knew each other for 8+ years and bring deep expertise in machine learning, high-performance computing and developer experience.

Sri was an ML Lead at Grammarly and Microsoft, where he shipped LLMs and personalization systems used by millions of users across Office, Bing, and Grammarly. His work on personalization drove 300% retention growth for Grammarly Keyboard and scaling models to 40M+ DAUs. He has published at top ML conferences such as ACL and holds multiple patents in real-time ML.

The idea for Moss came from our deep frustration with how slow “intelligent” systems actually felt in practice. While building large-scale agentic systems at Microsoft and Grammarly, we kept hitting the same wall - retrieval lag that made even the smartest models feel lifeless. Through evolution, humans are wired to expect instant replies; when AI hesitates, it breaks the illusion of intelligence. We started Moss to fix that by collapsing the multi-hop retrieval stack into a real-time, local-first runtime that lets AI think and respond at the speed of thought.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7-PrunZVXTo>

### **Who is it for?**

launches.title: JSX Tool: In-Browser React IDE
launches.tagline: The AI first IDE for React development
launches.body:
**tl;dr**

JSX Tool is an in-browser IDE that creates a common language between developers and AI for building React UIs. Click any element in the browser to jump straight to the relevant line of code and edit it yourself, or provide precise context to an LLM to make updates.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JIIXvN7vhrs

---

---

---

**The Problem**

LLMs have transformed how we write code, yet they consistently struggle with precise UI updates. The common belief is that AI simply doesn’t do well with visual tasks, but the real problem is that we're asking LLMs to understand UI without giving them proper context. They’re great at vibe styling but not great at producing precise UIs.

When you prompt an LLM about styling or component changes today, you're describing visual elements through text alone. It's like giving directions without a map. Meanwhile, developers juggle between browser DevTools, their code editor, screenshot tools, and component explorers just to gather enough context to make AI useful for these kinds of tasks.

**Our Solution**

JSX Tool addresses this by letting you click on any element and prompt your LLM with precise DOM context, the exact source component, its styles, and its position in the React hierarchy. Everything happens in one place: inspect, prompt, edit, and see changes instantly. 

And when AI suggestions aren't quite right, our full IDE is right there in the browser with that same context, so you can jump to the exact line of code you want to edit with a single click. You get the benefits of AI, while keeping the creative control and the nuanced decision-making that UI development demands.

Now developers and AI models share a common language for UI; both can reference the exact same visual elements with clarity, turning LLMs from guessing machines into powerful UI collaborators.

**@Tagging:** In your prompts, you can either type @ and click on a section of your webpage to reference another element relative to the one you’re focused on OR you can type @/ to mention files and directories you want the LLM to have as context in your prompt.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95312&key=user_uploads/3082625/2b76e7e0-6efc-4bb5-8b16-86f1cffd6f08)

**CSS Editor:** JSX Tool has a CSS editor that is nearly as feature-complete as the native CSS style editors found in browser element inspectors. Instead of applying your changes to a single element, you can see how your change to a line of JSX code would be applied globally.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95312&key=user_uploads/3082625/f911aeb0-3a85-4e30-9042-d49fd4a06d61)

**LSP Integrations:** JSX Tool ships with a lightweight IDE for manually editing code, but still an IDE that does some heavy lifting. The JSX Tool IDE integrates in language servers for common React development tasks, so you can have things like type-checking, auto-complete, and linting upon save. We currently ship with LSPs for Typescript, Tailwind, ESLint, and Prettier.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95312&key=user_uploads/3082625/57a590b7-b2c0-41e1-90c3-336c839b7219)

To learn more or start using the extension, go to [jsxtool.com](https://jsxtool.com)!

_Note: IDE features are currently in app review and will be available in our next release._

**Team**

Jamie and Dan grew up in New York City and have been working on projects together for nearly 20 years. Before JSX Tool, we most recently built a mobile app for bypassing news site paywalls.

Jamie is a second-time YC founder. Prior to starting JSX Tool, he worked as a Software Engineer at YCombinator on their investor software. He previously co-founded Cheqout, a restaurant technology company that was a part of the YC W21 batch. Prior to his first startup, Jamie worked on Airbnb's China Risk Team.

Jamie has had a deep interest in higher-order and visual programming for a while. He previously built a version control system to diff and merge structured, non-textual assets. Many of the technical problems encountered in that project were very similar to those encountered in JSX Tool.

Dan worked most recently as a Senior Software Engineer at Everblue, where he led engineering teams building workflow applications to power US government systems. Prior to that, he worked as a Senior Cloud Engineer at Sela US. He got his start in tech in the world of React and has since returned to his roots. In a former life, he was a Chef at a James Beard award-winning restaurant.

launches.title: Linzumi: team chat for directing AI coding agents
launches.tagline: Team chat for directing dozens of AI coding agents
launches.body:
# Hi everyone, I'm Sean, and I’m launching Linzumi today

**Linzumi is the team chat your engineering team uses to direct dozens of AI coding agents at once.** Kick off work, review it, ship it: all from chat. Try it at <https://linzumi.com>.

> For a limited time, every team chat account also gets free daily access to state of the art open-weights intelligence, GLM 5.2 at high speed, through our partnership with [Wafer.ai](http://Wafer.ai).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EM53ACaIHyg>

## The problem

The bottleneck in software has moved. Execution is basically free now: AI agents can write, test, and ship code 24/7. _The new constraint is human decisions and verification_. Whoever surfaces the right decision to the right person at the right moment unlocks 10x throughput. Whoever doesn't watches their agent fleet stall.

If you've ever tried to keep three coding agents productive at once, you know the feeling. You jump between PR tabs, miss approvals buried in Slack, and find one agent has sat idle for 20 minutes waiting on a one-line decision. It's a fascinating moment to be building software: vastly easier and vastly harder at the same time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103435&key=user_uploads/19683/9019e12e-5088-4b41-9321-28a417dade5a)

## How Linzumi works

Connect your machine, kick off work in chat, and review what every agent is doing from your laptop, your phone, or the coffee line. Works with Codex today, Claude Code coming soon. Your teammates see it all too: agent work is no longer buried in invisible terminals.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AQP5tQGZ9Jc>

But the real unlock is underneath. As your team works, Linzumi keeps every decision close to the work itself: what to build, why it changed, who approved it, and what the agents should do next. The decision inbox surfaces only the calls that need a human, so instead of reconstructing context from terminals, PRs, chats, and memory, your team has one shared place to steer the whole fleet.

_Continuous Context Compilation_

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TNJbWKYiDyc>

## Backstory

I'm a 3x YC founder. Before Linzumi I was at OpenAI on post-training and alignment research, where I worked on systems for making models follow written specs and produce more reliable reasoning. Working with coding agents on my own projects showed me the same kind of coordination problem at the team level: the agents could execute, but the bottleneck was deciding what should happen next and checking whether the result matched intent.

The mission now is to make everyone the CEO of their own 1,000-agent company: able to direct more work, make better decisions, and become the best version of themselves as a builder.

When you combine that shared context with calibrated decisions, even the smallest form factor can do surprising amounts of work, like shipping a customer feature from your phone on the way to the meeting.

_Hands-free work_

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pmqf3kwuOqI>

## What we're asking for

If you run AI coding agents (or want to), try Linzumi at <https://linzumi.com>. It's free to get started and we'd love your feedback.

We're especially looking for:

• Engineering teams running multiple coding agents who want to scale to dozens (honestly, thousands by end of year)

• Founders who feel like the bottleneck in their own dev cycle

• Anyone curious about better human-agent coordination for company-scale work

DM me on X (@sgrove) or email [sean@linzumi.com](mailto:sean@linzumi.com). I read every reply.

launches.title: Waddle Labs - Agents that control robots
launches.tagline: Claude Code for robotics - prompt your robot to do physical tasks
launches.body:
Waddle is the Claude Code for robotics. Connect our API to your robot and type a prompt, then our agents write code to achieve the task in \~20 minutes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107821&key=user_uploads/2132817/afc74f28-33c6-450c-80c3-7f2d263f213d)

### **Our Hypothesis**

Robot intelligence today depends either on large end-to-end VLAs or classical approaches.

\- VLAs are difficult to customise and steer, require huge amounts of data to train, and don’t yet generalise across embodiments and environment. They face limited deployment.

\- Meanwhile, classical approaches are widely deployed for their reliability and explicit control, but are often brittle and costly to redevelop in new setups.

_Does this tradeoff have to be inevitable?_

**Our hypothesis:** By using agents to control robots, we combine the generalisation of VLAs with the speed and reliability of classical approaches. 

### **Our Solution**

Our agents decomposes a goal into subtasks, and completes each subtask by viewing camera feeds, writing control code, and calling models like VLAs. The agent outputs a program that you can run and iterate on by talking to our agents. 

**Where we've been using Waddle internally:**

\- **Create a working policy in 20 minutes** ("Write a program to package the box")

\- **Generate data for model training** ("Pick and place lego bricks at random positions 1000 times")

\- **Facilitate robotics auto-research** ("I am tuning a policy overnight. Reset the scene after each trial”)\
\
Because our agents are LLMs, they inherit properties of the underlying models. Agents and the code they write are inherently generalist, so they work with any robot and any environment without additional data. Moreover, agents excel at long-horizon planning and can decompose a physical goal into subtasks, verify each stage, and re-plan on failure.

**Interested in trying our agents via our preview API?** Sign up at \[our website\](<https://www.waddlelabs.ai/>) or email [founders@waddlelabs.ai](mailto:founders@waddlelabs.ai)

### **Our Research**

Waddle's agents enable new forms of scaling that we are very excited about:

\- **Scaling compositional generalization:** Our agent first wrote the “fold_grasp” skill while flipping a package; another agent later used it to fold a t-shirt. Over time, agents accumulate a library of skills, enabling future agents to compose them and achieve harder tasks.

\- **Scaling multi-robot cooperation:** Imagine an entire fleet of robots collaborating to achieve a task. For VLAs, this is a nightmare. For Waddle, simply hook up more agents. A master agent spawns subagents, coordinating multiple robots working concurrently.

\- **Scaling from scale:** We evaluated Opus 4.8, Fable 5, and GPT 5.6 Sol on a suite of manipulation tasks: larger models with larger thinking budgets consistently produce better policies. As foundation models improve, so do our robots.

### **The Team**

We are @Yiding Song (Vincent) and @Hanming Ye. We met at MIT’s Research Science Institute, where Vincent was working on multimodal astrophysics models and Hanming was researching topology in the math department. Since then, we’ve become roommates at Harvard where we are either doing ML research or breaking robots - usually both.

There will be millions of robots in the future. Our mission is to enable everyone to take part in building them.

launches.title: Quotient Labs: Stop overpaying Claude for tokens you don't need
launches.tagline: We cut your Claude Code costs by 47% in one line of install. Same models, same workflow, half the price.
launches.body:
**TLDR**: **Tokenmaxxing is out. Tokenminning is in.** Quotient Labs sits on top of Claude Code and reduces the amount of context you pay for—without changing your models, prompts, projects, or workflow. Across real, multi-step developer workflows, we’ve benchmarked **47% lower token cost with no measured quality loss.** Get started today at <https://www.quotientlabs.com/>.

**The Problem**

Coding agents accumulate a lot of context.

Every file read, search result, test run, tool output, generated plan, and conversation turn gets added to the session. As the session grows, this history is repeatedly re-read (and re-billed) long after it has stopped being useful in its original form. The result? **You’re overpaying Claude for tokens your agent never needed.**

**Fermat’s Last Token** (our main product) sits on top of Claude Code and optimizes what enters and remains in your model’s context. We do this in four ways:

1. **Faster, more cost-efficient agent tools** that batch operations and return compact, information-dense results.
2. **Bash output compression** that preserves the useless parts of long command and test outputs while removing the bloat.
3. **Live text compression** that removes the information-sparse and irrelevant tokens in conversation turns before they ever compound in cost. 
4. **Idle context optimization** that compresses older conversation history as the prompt cache expires (this is more often than you think; only 5 minutes TTL) while preserving the freshest context verbatim.

The important part: **you keep using Claude Code exactly as you do today.**

**Observability**: See real-time estimated cost and savings down to the session and request level, as well as manage your organizations and users, in the user dashboard: <https://console.quotientlabs.com/>. 

**Ready to go in 30 seconds.** Install Fermat, sign in, and continue using Claude Code normally:

**curl -fsSL [https://downloads.quotientlabs.com/fermat/install.sh](https://downloads.quotientlabs.com/fermat/install.sh) | bash && fermat login**

**Fermat is compatible with both CLI and the VS Code extension.** Your existing projects, prompts, models, integrations, and interface are untouched.

You can bypass Fermat (if you really want) on a particular chat any time with _claude --vanilla._ You can also fully uninstall in one line with _fermat uninstall_ (though we don’t recommend either :)).

**Our ask**

We’re looking for devs and engineering teams who use Claude Code heavily, especially on long-running, tool-intensive engineering tasks. 

We’d love to get feedback on where Fermat helps the most, where compression could be better, and any features or changes you’d like to see.

Get started: <https://quotientlabs.com/>

Or message us directly: [founders@quotientlabs.com](mailto:founders@quotientlabs.com)

**Founders**

Before Quotient Labs, we’ve been at Stanford (BS+MS CS/AI), industry (Apple, AWS, Accenture) and in academia (with multiple publications).

launches.title: RunAnywhere: The default way to run On-Device AI at scale
launches.tagline: One SDK + Control Plane to Deploy, Route, Update, and Observe On-Device AI – Offline-First, Hybrid-Smart, Fleet-Managed
launches.body:
We're [Sanchit](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sanchitmonga22/) and [Shubham](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shubham-malhotra-fg890a23a/), co-founders of [RunAnywhere](https://runanywhere.ai/) (W26).

**TL;DR:** Run Multi-modal AI fully on-device with one SDK and manage model rollouts + policies from a control plane.

We are already live and open source with [**\~10.1k stars on GitHub**](https://github.com/RunanywhereAI/runanywhere-sdks).

<https://youtu.be/N3x2bs4ri68>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97041&key=user_uploads/725397/86d47939-7caf-4e0f-8575-045ca2fd22bc)

### The Problem

Edge AI is inevitable — users want instant responses, full privacy (health, finance, personal data), and AI that actually works on planes, subways, or spotty rural connections.

But shipping it today is brutal:

* Every device (iPhone 14 vs Android flagship vs low-end) has wildly different memory, thermal limits, and accelerators.
* Teams waste quarters rebuilding model download/resume/unzip/versioning, lifecycle (load/unload without crashing), multi-engine wrappers (llama.cpp, ONNX, etc.), and cross-platform bindings
* No real observability — you're blind to fallback rates, per-device perf, crashes tied to model version

**Result:** most teams either give up on local AI or ship a brittle, hacked-together experience.

### The Solution: Complete AI Infrastructure

RunAnywhere isn't just a wrapper around a model. It is a full-stack infrastructure layer for on-device intelligence.

**1. The "Boring" Stuff is Built-in** We provide a unified API that handles model delivery (downloading with resume support), extraction, and storage management. You don't need to build a file server client inside your app.

**2. Multi-Engine & Cross-Platform** We abstract away the inference backend. Whether it's llama.cpp or ONNX etc, you use one standard SDK.

* iOS (Swift)
* Android (Kotlin)
* React Native
* Flutter

**3. Hybrid Routing (The Control Plane)** We believe the future isn't "Local Only"—it's **Hybrid**. RunAnywhere allows you to define policies: try to run the request locally for zero latency/privacy; if the device is too hot, too old, or the confidence is low, automatically route the request to the cloud.

![Voice AI Pipeline Demo](/media/?type=post&id=97041&key=user_uploads/725397/dfe1b180-e5d8-4c59-a4e8-2109d9f903f2)

### Quick Links

* **OSS SDKs:** [github.com/RunanywhereAI/runanywhere-sdks](https://github.com/RunanywhereAI/runanywhere-sdks) (star if it vibes!)
* **Full Docs:** [docs.runanywhere.ai](https://docs.runanywhere.ai)
* **Website:** [runanywhere.ai](https://runanywhere.ai)

**Try our demo apps:**

* [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.runanywhere.runanywhereai)
* [iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/runanywhere/id6756506307)

### Our Ask

We're in full execution mode post-launch and hunting design partners + early feedback:

* Building voice AI, offline agents, privacy-sensitive features (health/enterprise/consumer), or hybrid chat in your mobile/edge app?
* Want to eliminate cloud inference costs for repetitive queries while keeping complex ones fast?
* Have a fleet where OTA model updates + observability would save you engineering months?

**Get in touch:**

* Drop us a line: [san@runanywhere.ai](mailto:sanchit@runanywhere.ai)
* Book a quick call: [calendly.com/sanchitmonga22](https://calendly.com/sanchitmonga22)
* Or just tell us what sucks about your current on-device AI stack — honest war stories help us prioritize.

Excited to hear what you're building and how we can make on-device AI actually shippable at scale.

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** _Review is an open-source desktop app designed to give you confidence in your code. Critique interactive visualizations, diffs, and agent traces, all from one interface. It’s like Cursor, but purpose-built for code review._

**Our Ask:** Try our app on your toughest code reviews; it is most illuminating for large, complicated changes. [Download the app](https://install.dev.fast/), [star the repo](https://github.com/devdotfast/review), & ask your questions on our [Discord](https://discord.gg/dev-fast)!

**Demo Video:** <https://youtu.be/mDgxhzrFi2Y>

**The Problem:**

No one knows how much code we should be reading these days.

It feels tedious and old-fashioned to manually comb through thousands of lines of changes, and yet irresponsible to merge code you can’t confidently describe.

We’ve lost touch with how our own systems work.

Building a company is a long game. Development is an iterative process. It takes accountability and code comprehension at every stage to build a great product that customers can count on ([ex 1](https://www.geoffreylitt.com/2026/07/02/understanding-is-the-new-bottleneck), [ex 2](https://margaretstorey.com/blog/2026/02/09/cognitive-debt/)).

**Our Solution:**

Before AI, staff engineers understood massive software systems even when they didn’t have time to read all contributed code. They prioritized without sacrificing complexity by:

\- Scrutinizing RFCs and architecture diagrams

\- Skipping low-impact PRs

Review treats you like a staff engineer. You can think of it as a ‘Cursor for code review.’ It helps you build programmatic, customizable RFCs from your PRs using coding agents.

Instead of reviewing 1000+ line diffs you:

1\. Consult a variety of interactive diagrams built on our SDK:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112248&key=user_uploads/2724635/4db58f4d-cdcc-4825-966d-c92ffcfedeba)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112248&key=user_uploads/2724635/d0b141ce-fcb3-4392-b59f-6d16e4f10f1a)

launches.title: Carson: More secure than OpenClaw, More capable than Cowork
launches.tagline: An AI agent with enterprise-grade security that generates custom, task-specific interfaces.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** AI agents are trapped in chat bubbles. Carson breaks free by generating dynamic interfaces like research dashboards or slide editors, customized to your current task. Carson is built for problem solvers pushing the bounds of AI in sales, marketing, and ops, with enterprise-grade security baked in.

**Our ask:** Sign up to use Carson today at [usecarson.com](http://usecarson.com), it's free for your first 7 days.

**Demo Video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=23sZGNMz3PU>

### The Problem:

AI tools today force you to choose between power and safety:

**1) Openclaw is powerful but insecure** ([example](https://x.com/summeryue0/status/2025774069124399363))**:**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98162&key=user_uploads/2724635/b2f3f2f6-a15c-437b-840a-e8e2f075c2d4)

**2) Claude Cowork is too limited:** Cowork is useful, but it could do much more. For example, if you use Cowork to source candidates, you need to bounce between LinkedIn, email, and the desktop app. Its permissions system is also clunky: you either approve every single action manually or skip permissions entirely with YOLO mode.

On some level security & autonomy are fundamental tradeoffs, but better tools should exist.

### The Solution:

Carson’s UI is generative, which means it changes to suit your use-case. Let’s walk through a common workflow as an example: **sales.**

**Phase 1: Outbound**: Below, I first use Carson to research leads. It realizes that I want structured data, so it fills an editable spreadsheet with deep research. 

Once that’s ready, I ask it to help me draft emails. Instead of switching between my LinkedIn, research, and my email, Carson generates a unified email workspace with all three in one pane.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98162&key=user_uploads/2724635/4d5a7add-b0dd-4189-be0c-2f296cc24915)

**Phase 2: First Meeting Prep (“Vibe Sliding”):** when the emails turn into meeting invites, I can use Carson to generate a customized slide deck based on the response & deep research (complete with branding)! I can also “vibe slide” and make edits to the slides using natural language.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98162&key=user_uploads/2724635/c69368ec-fa33-4746-a005-ef640ff400d7)

**Phase 3: Automations:** Carson can create and run automations in natural language. In this case, I ask Carson to send slides to me on Slack every time a new intro meeting comes up:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98162&key=user_uploads/2724635/7ec59f08-0a16-4bb4-aefd-e686923d5a21)

### 

**Security Infrastructure**

**TL;DR: You can actually install Carson at work.**

We weren’t happy at all with the primitives out there on agentic security. The compromises range from the uncomfortable (granting broad access to your entire email & calendar) to deeply concerning (giving an agent secret keys and telling it “\_hey make no mistakes\_”).

Instead, Carson is built around a fine-grained authorization system. You can tell the agent “\_it’s ok to send emails to these addresses, but ask me before interacting with those other ones\_”, and it’s enforced at the runtime level – the agent literally cannot send emails to unintended recipients.

### **Our Asks:**

If you’ve felt that Claude Cowork could be more capable or felt scared to try OpenClaw at work, Carson is right for you.

Contact us at +1-614-984-8423 or at [sid@usecarson.com](mailto:sid@usecarson.com). We’ll come over and install Carson for you (if you ask nicely, there may be a bag of sumo oranges provided, too).

**The Team**

Alex, Sid, and Milan met doing college projects together at Harvard, and Sid and Ketan go way back (to elementary school).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98162&key=user_uploads/2724635/275c90fc-a5a9-4199-a657-221b81dee677)

launches.body:
👋 We're Nars and Nishant, founders of Skillsync (W26).

**TL;DR:** Skillsync lets you move your context (sessions, memory, and skills) across every coding agent you use, with nothing lost. Start in Claude Code, continue in Codex, sync it with your team. Say it once; every agent & teammate has it.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112177&key=user_uploads/2980881/daf33474-9f03-4b30-ae87-d2d5de4efb88)

AI chats are annoying. Your context is trapped inside whatever agent you're using. You plan everything out in the Claude app, then open Claude Code to build, and none of that thinking comes with you. Switch from Claude Code to Cursor or Codex and it's the same story: you start from zero, re-explaining everything. And sharing your best skills with your team means zip files and Slack messages nobody can find.

Skillsync is a **local-first desktop app** that frees your context from any single agent:

* 🔁 **Move a session between agents with nothing lost**, including the full conversation, reasoning, and tool history.
* 🧠 **KYC: Know Your Context.** Keep your skills and memory in one place, searchable from any agent via MCP.
* 👥 **Sync your skills across your team**, edit once and everyone stays current. No zip files, no stale copies.

Everything runs on your machine, so your context stays yours.

We spent years building open source payments infra that connected dozens of payment processors, and scaled it to 30k+ GitHub stars. Making all those systems talk to each other taught us what real interoperability takes.

**One more thing…** 

The hard part, the engine that translates sessions across different agent formats without losing anything, is **open source**. It's written in Rust and it's called **txcript:** <https://github.com/skillsynchq/txcript/>. Don't take our word for it: **read the code**.

We're on a mission to set your context free. If this resonates, try Skillsync at <https://skillsync.com>

You can also reach us at [founders@skillsync.com](mailto:founders@skillsync.com)

launches.title: Salus - Runtime guardrails that validate AI agent actions before they execute
launches.tagline: Salus checks your agent's actions, blocking incorrect ones and providing feedback to guide retries
launches.body:
### **TL;DR:**

**Salus is an API that wraps around your agent and checks its actions at runtime, blocking incorrect ones and providing immediate feedback to guide retries.**

We’re Kevin and Vedant, former roommates at Stanford who studied CS, now building Salus full-time.

### 😔**The problem:** 

Your agent processed a refund without looking up the order, costing you thousands. It emailed your top lead using hallucinated data, ruining the deal. You only found out three hours later from a support ticket or an angry email.

Evals, output scoring, and observability are all necessary—but all reactive. They can reduce the likelihood of these problems occurring, but there's no solution that inspects an action as it’s about to execute. Salus does that.

**Ask:** If you are deploying agents and want to improve their correctness we’d love to help. Book a demo [here](https://calendly.com/d/cycy-fbc-fyj/salus-demo), and we can onboard you immediately with just a pip install and a few lines of code.

### 💻 **Our Solution:** 

<https://youtu.be/uyl5NJTY5Cg>

**How Salus validates an action:**

1. Actions must be **grounded in evidence**: Salus maintains an evidence cache for each run that every proposed action is validated against. Evidence includes all outputs from prior tool calls and the entire conversation history.
2. It must **adhere to policy**: Write constraints in YAML, markdown, or plain English. Salus compiles them into runtime checks that are version-controlled, diffable, and shadow-testable
3. And **more**: PII detection, budget/loop protection, idempotency, human-in-the-loop escalation, content moderation

**Self-repairing:** When Salus blocks an action, the agent receives structured feedback to guide a retry. In our benchmarks, **58%** of blocked actions recover and complete the task correctly.

### 📊 **Benchmarks:** 

We tested Salus on τ²-bench and ODCV-Bench. On τ²-bench, agents with Salus follow policies more reliably, at up to **60% lower cost**. On ODCV-Bench, Salus **reduced misalignment by 52%** on average across 12 frontier models (see below).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97574&key=user_uploads/1940292/e48b27f6-2e13-4d40-a9a4-13135ff981bc)

### ➕ **Other Features:** 

While we believe the missing piece is runtime validation, we know **evals and observability** are crucial. That’s why we incorporate all three in **one centralized product**. Using templates and LLMs, we generate thousands of both adversarial and realistic evals that have full context of your agent’s domain.

Contact us: [founders@usesalus.ai](https://founders@usesalus.ai)

launches.title: IncidentFox. The AI SRE who never drops context.
launches.tagline: Auto-learns your stack, builds its own integrations, and gets smarter after every incident.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We're [Long](https://www.linkedin.com/in/long-yi-b221b2183/) and [Jimmy](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chiehmin-wei/) — co-founders of IncidentFox.

**TL;DR**

AI SRE tools fail without deep context about _your_ systems — and that context lives in integrations nobody has time to build. IncidentFox auto-discovers what each team needs, generates the integrations, and ships with 300+ tools built in. Setup takes less than a day, not months.

👉 Try it: <https://incidentfox.ai>

👉 Open source (Apache 2.0): <https://github.com/incidentfox/incidentfox>

👉 Launch video: <https://youtu.be/TaTpN0JwNYE>

**❌ The Problem: Without the right integrations, your AI has no context**

Every AI SRE tool connects to Slack, reads your Confluence, queries your Datadog. That part is solved.

Here's what isn't: when the AI actually needs to debug something, it doesn't have the right tools.

Your payments team runs a custom Kafka pipeline with internal dashboards. Your infra team uses a homegrown deployment system. Your ML team has proprietary model serving. Each team's stack is different — and the AI has no way to query any of it.

The traditional fix? Hand-build integrations (MCP servers) for every team.

But this creates a new problem:

* Who decides what integrations each team needs? You might know your own team's stack — but when you're debugging another team's service at 3 AM, you don't know theirs.
* So every team needs to sacrifice an engineer to build and maintain their own integrations. That's expensive, slow, and doesn't scale.
* Most teams never get around to it. The AI stays half-useful.

**Integration is the bottleneck.** Not the AI model. Not the monitoring data. The integrations.

**🦊 IncidentFox: We auto-build the integrations for you**

IncidentFox is an AI SRE that lives where your team already works — Slack, Microsoft Teams, or Google Chat. It doesn't just connect to your existing tools — it figures out what tools each team needs and builds them automatically.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97928&key=user_uploads/1146198/102ebfb0-a3c9-45c5-b993-89e39b94e13b)

**1. Auto-discovers and generates integrations**

IncidentFox analyzes your codebase, infrastructure, and incident history to identify gaps — then auto-generates the tools to fill them. No engineer needs to hand-build MCP servers. No team needs to sacrifice headcount on integration work.

A new team onboards? IncidentFox studies their stack and proposes tools specific to their services — with human approval before anything goes live.

**2. Per-team configuration — because every team is different**

Your payments team and your ML team don't use the same stack. Why would they use the same AI SRE config?

Each team gets their own:

* Tools — enable only what's relevant; disable what isn't
* Prompts — fully open source and exposed to engineers. Inject your domain knowledge directly
* Knowledge base — learned from that team's incidents, runbooks, and services

One team's "config drift" is another team's "model drift." IncidentFox understands the difference.

**3. Continuously evaluates and self-improves**

After every incident, IncidentFox:

* Detects gaps — "I couldn't query service X's health endpoint"
* Auto-generates the missing tool
* Evaluates its own investigation quality against the actual resolution
* Updates prompts and knowledge — with human review

It gets measurably better every week. Not because you tuned it — because it tuned itself.

**4. 300+ integrations included on day one**

While it auto-builds what's missing, you're not starting from zero. Kubernetes, AWS, Grafana, Prometheus, Datadog, Elasticsearch, PagerDuty, GitHub — all built in. Integration time is under a day, not months.

**🧠 Why this matters**

**Integrations** — Traditional: Hand-built per team. Each team sacrifices an engineer. IncidentFox: Auto-discovered and auto-generated. Human approves.

**Multi-team scaling** — Traditional: Breaks — you can't know every team's stack. IncidentFox: Per-team config. Each team's AI knows their stack.

**Domain knowledge** — Traditional: Black box prompts, hope it works. IncidentFox: Open source prompts. Engineers inject and edit freely.

**Over time** — Traditional: Stagnates unless manually updated. IncidentFox: Self-evaluates, finds gaps, improves continuously.

**Setup** — Traditional: Months of custom integration work. IncidentFox: < 1 day. 300+ tools out of the box.

**📊 Results**

* 85–95% reduction in alert noise through intelligent correlation
* Hours → minutes for incident investigation
* Zero-config onboarding — Docker in 5 min, production K8s in 30 min

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97928&key=user_uploads/1146198/844d70ec-e308-472c-9bc4-f212cd954153)

**🔒 Enterprise-ready, open-source**

* Open source — Apache 2.0, no vendor lock-in
* SOC 2 compliant, SSO/OIDC, RBAC, audit logs
* Self-hosted, on-prem, or managed SaaS
* Bring your own LLM keys (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, etc.)

**👬 The Team**

[**Jimmy (CEO)**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chiehmin-wei/) — Previously at Roblox, where he built social communication features (in-experience calling for 100M+ DAU). Before that, worked at Meta FAIR on multiparty conversational AI, with published research. Cornell CS. Serial founder — previously CTO at a startup in Outlier Ventures' DeFi accelerator.

[**Long (CTO)** ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/long-yi-b221b2183/)— Previously at Roblox, where he built database infrastructure supporting 100M+ daily active users on the Stateful Infra team. Experienced the chaos of on-call firsthand — which is why we're building this. Brandeis CS + Neuroscience + Business.

We've lived on both sides: Jimmy built the AI systems, Long was the SRE drowning in incidents. IncidentFox is what happens when you combine both.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97928&key=user_uploads/1146198/261f0711-50aa-4a0f-b6c9-9cdc7c853dbc)


**🙏 Our Asks**

* Try IncidentFox — self-serve at [incidentfox.ai](https://incidentfox.ai) or star us on [GitHub](https://github.com/incidentfox/incidentfox)
* Intros to engineering teams spending too much time on on-call
  * [Book a demo with us](https://calendly.com/d/cxd2-4hb-qgp/30-minute-demo-call-w-incidentfox)
* Feedback from SREs and infra engineers — [founders@incidentfox.ai](mailto:founders@incidentfox.ai)

Thanks for reading ❤️

launches.body:
> **TLDR:** Create an API sandbox with the environments your CI, tests, and evals need. Your coding agent can start the API sandboxes (e.g Linear, Slack, Datadog), run tests, and inspect state changes. Ask your agent about archal.ai!

Hi everyone, I'm Aidan, the founder of Archal. I previously built agent environments at Scale AI and I've been an avid developer for most of my life, which led me to the problem Archal poses to solve.

[https:/youtu.be/pUfu1RFDYVk](https://youtu.be/pUfu1RFDYVk)

**What we found**

Coding agents are getting much better at writing integrations, but testing those integrations is still painful. Many providers do not offer a usable sandbox, so developers fall back to throwaway accounts, shared test workspaces, or thin mocks. Those options are difficult to reset and make it hard to know whether an agent actually completed a task or only returned a plausible response.

As Adam Bender at Google put it, “But with 10x more code and 10x more services, integration tests are going to become the most important part of your quality strategy.” (Google, Software engineering is at the tipping point)

**How Archal works**

With all of this in mind, I built Archal for a starting point of how the next generation of devs will do QA. It's a tool focused on giving agent developers and integration engineers API sandboxes of the SaaS platforms they use in prod pipelines. With Archal, a developer or their coding agent can start a sandbox, run the task, inspect what changed, and reset everything for the next test. We eliminate the need of separate test accounts, thin mocks and stubs, as well as overburdening rate limits on provider-owned sandboxes.

**Our ask**

We're giving out $20 in Archal credits to each new developer that signs up and starts a sandbox. We’d love for you to give it a try and give us feedback, cheers to making testing easier in the era of coding agents!

We’re [Mitch](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mitchellradhuber/) and [Shipra](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shipra-jha-9b021859/) - before Corelayer, we built data infrastructure at Goldman Sachs where we spent many late nights and weekends debugging systems that processed 100s of billions of rows a day.

**TL;DR**

When you’re on call in data-heavy, regulated industries like fintech, healthcare, or insurance, you need to inspect underlying data to debug production issues. We built a platform that monitors both infrastructure and data for anomalies and uses AI agents to debug and suggest fixes in minutes.

[Corelayer Launch Video](https://youtu.be/yFZKJ9QRrr4)

**On-call support is painful and expensive**

All engineers hate being on call. Production issues kill velocity, erode user trust, and become more and more costly as companies scale.

Fortune 100s spend **$100M+/year** on first-line-of-defense production support.

Smaller companies can’t afford to burn **scarce engineering resources** on time-consuming support and maintenance.

**The (sensitive) data problem**

If you’re a backend engineer at a fintech, you probably own a service that queries data, applies some business logic, and stores the result somewhere (i.e., a data pipeline).

When this service is running in production, you’ll see two failure modes:

1. Exceptions in logs and/or failing jobs
2. Bad data produced by your service

“Bad data” can mean anything from incorrect values to entirely missing or duplicated rows.

**This is really common** in certain products and industries, but you’re totally blind to these errors without monitoring data for anomalies and querying data while debugging.

In regulated environments where this problem is prevalent, **production data is sensitive**, which is another constraint we have to solve for.

**Corelayer solves this**

We continuously monitor logs, metrics, **and data** for anomalies and use AI agents to debug, root-cause, and suggest fixes for issues.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=96772&key=user_uploads/2897480/fce0b569-7a89-41f5-8225-625e86092a04)

We also filter out false positives and group related issues to reduce alert noise.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=96772&key=user_uploads/2897480/6b91dd40-c7c7-4ca9-97a4-f80eaaff537d)

Every team is different. We take feedback from human engineers so our agents learn your systems and improve over time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=96772&key=user_uploads/2897480/f5384b34-039b-40f5-ba00-4c1ede356893)

Data is especially sensitive in regulated industries. We’re SOC 2 compliant, offer **BYOC and** **on-prem deployments**, flexible LLM inference options, and expose an audit trail of each step performed by the agent with citations.

**Our Asks**

Does your team deal with data or integrations and spend more time on production support than you’d like? [Let’s chat](https://cal.com/mitchrad/30min). 

Can you connect us with an engineering leader at a finserv, fintech, healthcare, or insurance company? Reach out at [founders@corelayer.com](mailto:founders@corelayer.com).

Thank you!

launches.title: Replicas - End-to-End Background Coding Agents
launches.tagline: Background coding agents for engineering teams
launches.body:
Hi there, I'm Connor from [Replicas](https://replicas.dev/) :)

Recently, you might have seen Stripe and Ramp release blogs outlining their in-house background coding agents. This showed us that background agents, with the proper tooling, can be relied on to ship critical production code.

Replicas is a background coding agent that can run your codebase locally.

We’re used by 20+ YC startups at all team sizes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99287&key=user_uploads/1688990/b35f4253-6fd0-478b-a04f-26f73a18b625)

**The Problem**

Background coding agents are a huge productivity boost for clearing tickets and shipping faster.

The existing solutions - CC/Codex on Cloud, Cursor Agents - lock you into one harness and give you **no control over the environment**.

This defeats the entire point of "background" agents. A powerful background agent should run everything locally, verify its work, and iterate until it's satisfied.

**How Replicas Works**

**Replicas** helps you delegate to as many background agents as you need:

\- Bring your own Claude/Codex credentials

\- Each agent gets a sandbox VM with your code cloned

\- The agent installs deps, spins up databases, runs services, and verifies its work locally

\- When it's done, it opens a PR for you to review

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99287&key=user_uploads/1688990/e20b6968-523d-4376-a05c-ba175cc61611)

Replicas can be triggered from Slack, Linear, GitHub (PR reviews, CI/CD failures), the Dashboard, or API.

The biggest difference is **Environments**. You can configure the following:

\- Files

\- Env vars

\- Start hooks

\- Warm hooks

\- Skills/MCPs

It's built so that its flexible to any kind of codebase, allowing Replicas to run everything locally just like a human engineer would.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99287&key=user_uploads/1688990/df185d7b-b90e-455f-9ff7-10dcefcfd8c7)

Replicas can also create **Previews**:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99287&key=user_uploads/1688990/7be01ba9-b653-43f2-975d-234002802e15)

Meaning you can check out services (e.g web app on `3000`) running on the sandbox's VM from your computer with just a click :)

Check out this writeup for Replicas V1 for more details:

<https://www.replicas.dev/notes/replicas-v1>

**Demo Video**

<https://youtube.com/watch?v=uyH77T-pcXc>

**What's Next**

\- **Automations + API**: Improving our API and adding an automations menu, e.g having Replicas run every night.

\- **Recursive**: Replicas can break down super complex tasks by creating more Replicas instances.

\- **Lowering Latency**: For larger teams, improving our warm pool and snapshotting infrastructure to make spinning up Replicas feel _instant_ (more than it already does)

\- **Long-term Memory**

\- and what our customers ask for :p

**What I'm asking from you**

\- Sign up (<https://replicas.dev>) or reach out ([connor@replicas.dev](mailto:connor@replicas.dev))

\- Check out \[this writeup\](<https://www.replicas.dev/notes/replicas-v1>) for Replicas V1

\- Upvote if this resonates with you!

Hi, I’m Rob, the founder of Zenbu

## The problem

Coding agents are changing how software gets built, but they also create a new kind of complexity: running several agents in parallel, reviewing changes nobody wrote by hand, verifying their work, switching contexts, and keeping track of the codebase.

## The solution

Zenbu is an IDE for managing that complexity.

It’s built on top on Pi, the minimal, customizable coding agent. Around Pi, Zenbu adds an extensible IDE where everything is a plugin, including the tools for managing agents.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102484&key=user_uploads/3026245/3318eb29-4238-42d0-a338-9543b7e1fffd)

That matters because every developer and company works with agents differently. Instead of forcing one workflow, Zenbu lets the best solutions get built as plugins by developers and teams with their own needs. Over time, the best ways to work with agents become part of the shared foundation everyone can build on.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZUbY8zdv7Rc>

## About me

I build developer tools. I co-authored React Scan, an open source tool now at 22k GitHub stars and 800k weekly installs. I also worked at Vercel, where I joined the Next.js team and built an internal development environment.

Zenbu is the IDE I wanted for working with coding agents every day.

launches.tagline: A wizard sets up your telemetry every day. An agent investigates incidents and ships mergeable PRs.
launches.body:
Hey YC! We're Nicolò and Arseniy, co-founders of Superlog ([superlog.sh](https://superlog.sh/)).

**TL;DR:** Superlog is the observability tool you're not supposed to open. A wizard scans your repo and instruments it with OpenTelemetry, and re-runs daily to keep your logs, alerts, and dashboards in sync with your code. When something breaks, an agent investigates with full context and posts one mergeable PR per incident into Slack.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AeX3pnHCMHg>

## **The Problem**

Arseniy spent years at Datadog, getting paged during the night to debug production incidents. In our first startups, we tried Sentry, Datadog, Grafana, Dash0, and nothing was good enough. 

* **Setup never ends.** Proper telemetry takes days of manual work and breaks the moment you ship new features. Half the dashboards end up empty or outdated.
* **Alert fatigue is constant.** Sentry floods Slack with duplicates and no context. The Saturday #ops ping is the worst feeling of the week.
* **The bill climbs.** Datadog invoices keep growing while engineers still spend hours configuring dashboards, chasing three AWS metrics that disagree, and copy-pasting stack traces into Claude at 11pm.

## **Our Solution**

**1. Telemetry that sets itself up.** Tell your agent:

```
Run npx skills add superloglabs/skills --all and use the skills to install Superlog in this project
```

This skill instruments your code with native OTel SDKs: proper semantic conventions, service and environment tagging. We cover all failure modes, endpoint performance, usage per tenant, and LLM/upstream cost (by callsite, tenant, and model). We run observability check-ins that keep adding logs, alerts, and dashboards as your code grows.

**2. An agent that investigates and ships PRs.** Errors get prioritised and grouped into incidents. The agent investigates with full context (logs, traces, metrics, recent deploys) and either produces a short tested PR, or posts its findings and pulls in the engineers who own the system (based on docs, prior investigations, Slack threads). One mergeable PR per incident in Slack. Merge it, ignore it, or open it as a Claude Code/Codex session and tweak.

**3. No alert fatigue.** Our custom eval setup makes sure incident summaries in your #ops channel are dense and correct, with severity and impact upfront. Every LLM-enhanced metric ships with a confidence score, so wrong guesses don't get boosted.

The telemetry you get is vendor-neutral: you keep all the OTel logs, metrics, and traces we install, even if you choose to switch providers.

## **Where We're Going**

Every engineering team in the world burns nights and weekends debugging production. We want to delete that loop. Observability should install itself, alert intelligently, and fix what it can.

## **About Us**

* **Nicolò (CEO)** — ex-BCG, math olympiad winner, scaled two startups to millions in ARR, with international enterprise contracts at Bluco (McDonald’s, Volkswagen, Dufry, etc).
* **Arseniy (CTO)** — coding since 12yo, won school olympiads, worked on high-performance data systems at Datadog and built engineering teams from scratch at Bluco.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101239&key=user_uploads/1660276/b630a0c3-d186-4f4c-95c0-6832f7893f47)

## **Our Ask**

We'd love intros to:

* Engineering leaders drowning in Sentry alerts or Datadog bills
* Startups that rolled their own observability and want to throw it away

**Try it:** [superlog.sh](https://superlog.sh/)\

We’re [@Kaahan Radia](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/569532) and [@Parth Radia](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3206626) from Keyframe Labs. Our interactive video models bring your AI agents and applications to life.

You can try a video call for yourself here: <https://keyframelabs.com>. To get a sense for the interactivity and expressive range, try asking for a sad Shakespearean monologue. Or for a “funny” dad joke.

**But why video agents?**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99738&key=user_uploads/3206626/ad0420da-db57-4562-a1a4-b5db0b0de005)

Face-to-face interaction triggers responses that text and voice simply can’t. Video calls close more deals, language learning with video tutors outperforms audio-only, and human presence drives outcomes in high-stakes interactions (e.g., telehealth, tax prep).

Now that voice has emerged as a primary conversational interface across industries, video is the next leap. Developers and enterprises already use Keyframe to easily deploy photoreal, conversational humans to a wide variety of use cases, including:

* AI roleplay, for corporate training / learning and development
* AI recruiting, for interview practice and automated screenings
* Telehealth
* High-touch customer support
* AI sales and customer success reps
* Always-on digital twins of influencers, to scale engagement and hyper-personalize interactions

**How it works**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99738&key=user_uploads/3206626/34f670bd-7436-48e9-bd72-2d0f8bd73e44)

Super simple.

1. Connect your agent or LLM, or choose from our supported providers
2. Select a persona from our stock library
3. Drop the embed code into your application

Need a custom persona or more control? Custom personas are available on enterprise plans, and our SDKs let you roll your own implementation.

**Why Keyframe**

Our research goals from day one have been:

* Make meaningful progress towards beating the uncanny valley
* Run at real-time, with world-scale efficiency

The result:

* Industry-leading realism and concurrency limits
* At a fraction of the cost of competitors

**Get up and running**

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Mentlio is the engineering intelligence platform for the AI-coding era. We help engineering organizations cut AI costs by up to 30% and finally see what ROI that spend is actually producing. All without ever collecting your prompts or source code.

**Launch Video**

<https://youtu.be/-28j9HvTYV0>

**Problem**

Every engineering org is now an AI org. Token usage is growing exponentially, and so is the bill. The following questions have been largely unanswered:

* How can we cut our usage-based AI spend without bottlenecking usage or efficiency?
* What ROI are we getting for every dollar of AI spend?
* To what extent is AI-generated code creating quality debt?

Brian Armstrong recently laid out how Coinbase is reducing AI spend while token usage grows exponentially on X: better defaults, smarter routing, cache awareness, lean context, and full visibility into usage and impact. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111055&key=user_uploads/2693539/7bf48740-dd37-4015-9da9-ec0f9bd900ed)

Coinbase built a custom harness, LLM gateway, routing, and usage visibility internally. We believe they have the right thesis, but most engineering orgs don’t want to run on a custom harness. **Mentlio gives every eng team a better version of those savings & visibility without changing any workflows.**

**Solution**

Mentlio gives you:

1. **ROI.** We translate every PR into normalized units of work: Delivery Points. We consider associated spend, code reusability, and historical patches to turn "we spend $X on AI"  -> "we spend $X per impact point.” compared to industry data. 
2. **Cost intelligence + optimization.** See exactly where AI spend goes across teams, tools, and models. Optionally catch and cut waste across cache misses, oversized models on trivial tasks, bloated context and cut it without capping/bottlenecking accuracy. 
3. **Quality signal.** AI-assisted code that ships fast but breaks later isn't a win. We connect AI usage to delivery and quality outcomes so you can see the full picture

We’re the only platform with the above capabilities that never collects prompts or source code.

**Our Asks**

If you are or know a Head of Eng, VP Eng, CTO, or platform lead at a 15+ engineer org with real AI spend, reach out! You can book a demo at[ mentlio.com/intro](http://mentlio.com/intro) or reach us at [founders@mentlio.com](mailto:founders@mentlio.com).

**The Team**

Ashank and Ahmet met while studying Computer Science at Caltech while they were working part-time Founding Engineer roles at Series A and Seed stage startups. Ashank previously researched generative image AI & graph deep learning for pathology, genomics, and drug design at Dartmouth & Purdue and won internationally at the International Science & Engineering Fair & Junior Science & Humanities Symposium. Ahmet previously published his research in transformers and AI in IEEE, BMC AI, and ACM and also won internationally at the National AI Olympiad, International Science & Engineering Fair, and was named a Top 300 Science Scholar by Regeneron.

**TL;DR:** InsForge lets your AI coding agent deploy and operate the full backend (servers, database, auth, storage, and more) from one consistent CLI. Instead of stitching together separate tools and dashboards, your agent manage entire backend infrastructure end-to-end.

<https://youtu.be/7Bax5qz0IfM>

**The Problem**

The way software gets built is changing fast. Coding agents are now the primary builders, but every backend platform today was designed for human developers, with dashboards, manual configs, and workflows that require a person at every step.

We tried MCP servers like Supabase, Vercel, GitHub, and Context7, but kept running into the same problems: tools bloated the context window, payloads came back at 10K+ tokens, and core backend state like telemetry, configs, logs, and runtime behavior still wasn’t accessible in a way agents could reliably use.

**Our Solution**

So we built InsForge as one backend platform your coding agent can actually operate. Install our CLI and Skills with one command, and your coding agent can build, run, debug, and scale full-stack apps end to end on InsForge.

Every primitive returns structured outputs and readable errors the agent can act on. And because agents make mistakes, branching, scoped permissions, and reversible writes let you review or discard changes safely.

**Where We're Going**

We believe that coding agents won’t stop at writing code. They’ll run your entire application and infrastructure autonomously as well. For that to work, backend infrastructure needs to become agent-native: CLI-first, observable, permissioned, reversible, and designed around agents as operators.

**About Us**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101500&key=user_uploads/967495/90d7cdcf-0682-408c-bf3c-c5f192edf89b)

* **Hang (CEO)** — ex-Amazon PM, previously professional League of Legends player.
* **Tony (CTO)** — ex-Databricks network infrastructure engineer.

**Our Ask**

1. **Try it and break it**: [**insforge.dev**](http://insforge.dev). If you found there’s anything missing or you think some features are poorly designed, let us know! We read every piece of feedback. We’re also open source, here’s our [**GitHub repo**](https://github.com/InsForge/InsForge).
2. **Design partners**: if you want your coding agent to handle everything, and believe that’s the future, drop a comment or email [**founders@insforge.dev**](mailto:hang.huang@insforge.dev). We'll get you set up directly.
3. **Intros:** we're a day-0 infra company, so we need to find top developers before they get locked in elsewhere. If you know any developers or founders just / about to get started, we’d love an intro!

name: Rindler
long_description:
We build Maxxwell, a desktop app for people who run several coding agents at once.

Past two or three sessions, you become the bottleneck. Every session asks you something, most of it small, and you spend the day answering instead of deciding. It is also hard to tell which sessions are making progress, which are stuck on something trivial, and which have quietly started building the wrong thing.

Maxxwell puts every session in one window and marks each one working, idle, or waiting on you. On top of that sits an orchestrator, a real coding-agent session of its own that reads the others and reports back. You talk to it instead of to twelve terminals. It tells you what landed, what it decided for you, and what actually needs your call.

Every worker is your own tool, unmodified. Claude Code, Codex and Cursor Agent run in real terminal sessions you can attach to and take over at any point

launches.title: Rindler - Turn Any Website Into An API For AI Agents
launches.tagline: Reliable web actions for AI agents, without integrations or scripts
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Rindler turns websites into deterministic APIs for AI agents. We map a site once into screens, actions, and structured outputs, so agents can read data and take actions quickly and reliably.

**Ask:** If you’re building an agent that needs to browse the web, compare products, fill forms, search listings, use authenticated portals, or act on third-party websites without an API, we’d love to help.

<https://youtu.be/V_nCIxYD-so>

## Problem

More products are starting to depend on AI agents that can do real work on the web: shop across retailers, pull housing listings, use job boards, submit forms, monitor prices, update back-office systems, and operate inside customer portals.

But most browser agents still treat every website visit like a new puzzle. On every run, they need to decipher the page, infer what matters, decide what to click, and recover when the page behaves differently.

That works for demos, but it breaks down in production. Real websites have pop-ups, login gates, cookie banners, bot defenses, slow-loading forms, dynamic filters, fragile dropdowns, layout changes, and pages that look similar but behave differently.

The result is slow execution, high token cost, and workflows that are hard to trust.

## Solution

Rindler maps websites into deterministic APIs for agents.

Instead of forcing an agent to re-explore a site every time, Rindler captures the site as structured screens, available actions, and typed outputs. Agents can then call actions like **search,** **add_to_cart**, or **download_records,** depending on the mapped site.

At runtime, Rindler handles the browser work through a remote MCP endpoint:

* Returning structured data
* Applying dynamic filters
* Managing popups, bot defenses, and layout changes
* Supporting authenticated flows

## Background

We started Rindler because “AI agent uses a browser” is compelling, but the current browser-agent loop is too brittle for teams building real products.

If an agent needs to use the same third-party site hundreds or thousands of times, it should not have to rediscover that site from scratch on every run.

Rindler is still a work in progress. Some sites map cleanly, others require more in-depth mappings, and bot-defended or logged-in sites may need a one-time credential or cookie capture.

We’re looking for feedback from founders building products where reliable web actions are part of the core workflow.

If there’s a website you wish your agent could use reliably, send it to us!

launches.tagline: The Git forge for agent-scale teams
launches.body:
Software development is becoming much more parallel. Coding agents let a team have dozens or hundreds of related changes moving at the same time, creating more branches, reviews, CI runs, and automation than existing workflows were designed to absorb.

Today, we’re opening GitCafe in public beta. It is a Git forge built for teams where humans and coding agents may ship hundreds or thousands of changes a day. We’re building the hosting, review, CI, security, and automation layer for that way of working.\
\
Hundreds of users are already on GitCafe, and we’re currently running trials with roughly a dozen YC companies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109445&key=user_uploads/1920545/eecbfb4f-82f1-4660-8ee8-aeea5273a8b9)

Generating code is only part of the problem. Teams still need to understand what is changing, review it safely, keep CI moving, catch security issues, and coordinate work without becoming overwhelmed.

We’re not building GitCafe because putting repositories, code review, and CI in one product is new. We’re building it because we believe the workload those systems need to support is about to change dramatically.

We started by rebuilding the Git infrastructure itself. Now we’re closing the product gap feature by feature.

Recently, we added secret scanning, Buildkite and Harmont CI support, stacked diffs with Jujutsu and Sapling integration, and beta support for GitHub Actions.

These are foundational capabilities, not the destination. Building them on infrastructure we own gives us a base we can keep extending for higher-volume, agent driven development.

The honest version is that GitCafe is behind GitHub today. GitHub has spent more than a decade building an enormous product, and GitCafe does not yet have every workflow, administrative control, or integration that mature teams need. Some features are missing, some are experimental, and some edges are rough. We expect to earn the broader product surface, not claim it on day one.

We’re opening GitCafe now because the fastest way to improve it is to put it in the hands of teams doing real work.

If your team is already using coding agents heavily, try GitCafe at <https://git.cafe> and tell us where the workflow breaks down.\
\

launches.body:
Cloud coding agents are painful to set up, lacking ergonomics, and don't allow you to move as fast as possible. We let you bring your local set up to the cloud.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108274&key=user_uploads/2563241/28db62de-d65b-4498-84ac-12e2683c65f2)

**The Problem** 

In the next 10 years the best software startups will be those who can effectively deploy tokens. 

Right now that's significantly harder than it needs to be. If you’ve ever ran multiple agents locally you immediately know this pain.

Laptop crashes, wrangling gitwork trees, juggling ports, and more headaches.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108274&key=user_uploads/2563241/6f320e85-ccbb-4fb4-a5e9-6ec3cb0206c7)

So cloud is the obvious answer right? 

But setting up with these existing providers is quite a hassle, and oftentimes they miss some key feature that your local config has.

**What we do**

We deploy software factories into businesses that want to **tokenmaxx** but don't have the time or the resources to set up the infrastructure.

During onboarding, we transfer all of your local sessions and MCP servers to Hoplite, meaning you can pick up right from where you left off. We also configure all the required dependencies and CLIs that your projects require, letting you see instant previews of what your agent is doing.

Our bet is that as models improve, we’re going to start caring less about the code that they output (we’ll implicitly trust it), and shift our focus towards the product itself. Hence, a platform that prioritizes iteration on product rather than code will ultimately win. 

We also have an iMessage integration so you can prompt on the go.

We installed in our first business last week and we saw an immediate result, from sentry logs going from largely ignored to fully proactive PRs when something breaks. 

They have significantly faster iteration cycles and lower priority tickets have been continuously getting merged. 

They wanted faster iterations but didn't have the infrastructure to support a software factory, so we went in and built it.

If this sounds like you reach out! 

P.S. – If you love Vim, this is for you. It was built with keyboard navigation in mind 🙂

demo vid: <https://x.com/ryan_morr/status/2078240892738224292?s=20>

sign up: <https://hoplite.sh>

**How we got here**

Previously, we were building an agentic harness for financial markets; letting retail investors trade with AI. The product worked well, but we never truly had founder market fit. 

We found that our true passion was in talking to founders and developers – and oftentimes when pitching our old product, I’d spend 5x longer explaining our potential pivot 😅

And so we set out to commercialize a product that we’d built internally, one that’d let us deploy the $1.5 million in OpenAI credits effectively.

**Our Ask:** Let us Collison install! Bence and I will come to your apartment and set up everything for you (and bring some matcha & assorted sweet treats). We want to build the best possible product for developers to move faster and care deeply about peoples setups. Partially because we have very strong opinions of our own… 

**The Team** 

Bence & I are both from Ireland 🇮🇪. We met in college in a course called Immersive Software Engineering. 

We have been building projects & doing freelance work tg for the past 2 years, but got sick of building other people's visions. 

We previously interned at AWS (Bence) & [@Stripe](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/240) (Ryan). After that experience, we were fed up and decided to drop out to build. 

We are best friends & just want to build a product that people truly love.

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Marinos and Hudson, co-founders of Prized.

**TL;DR:** Prized gives developers a dedicated devbox in the cloud that still feels local. Your files stay synced to a real folder, ports show up on [localhost](http://localhost), and coding agents keep running when you close your laptop.

Launch video: <https://youtu.be/JmaxNhEdLdc>

**The problem**

Coding agents can work for hours now. But only if you keep your laptop open.

You start a refactor, a migration, or a big build. Then you need to leave. Close the lid and the agent dies with it.

You can move everything to a VM, but now you're doing remote dev. Your files live somewhere else. Your ports need forwarding. Your terminal disappears when the connection drops.

Remote development still feels remote.

it shouldn't…

**The solution**

With Prized, one command puts your project on a dedicated devbox without giving up local development:

* **Real files on your Mac.** Prized syncs both ways into a normal folder, so everything keeps working the way it already does.


* [**Localhost**](http://Localhost)** stays [localhost](http://localhost)**. Servers running on the box appear on your Mac automatically, including loopback-only services and hot reload.


* **Sessions stay alive.** SSH lands in a persistent terminal session on the box, so disconnecting or closing your laptop doesn't stop the work.


* **Compute grows with the task.** Resize the box without rebuilding your environment or moving your project again.


* **Secrets stay out of the agent's hands.** For brokered secrets, the agent only sees a placeholder.

**The team**

We worked together at Gander (F24) building fleet management software for private jets. After the company's acquisition by Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR), Marinos continued school at Stanford, and Hudson went on to be an engineer at Suno.

We built Prized for ourselves after getting tired of having to keep our laptops cracked open all the time. A raw VM kept the process alive but gave up the local workflow we actually wanted.

Check Prized out at [https://prized.dev](https://prized.dev/), or reach out at [founders@prized.dev](mailto:founders@prized.dev).

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Marinos and Hudson, co-founders of Prized.

**TL;DR:** Prized lets anyone at your company build and ship secure internal tools with AI. Company data comes pre-connected and scoped to what each person should see, every access is audited, and finished tools deploy behind your company's sign-in.

**Launch video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WILimoqemD4>

**The problem**

Building software has never been easier. And the people who need internal tools most, in ops, support, and finance, are done waiting on engineering.

So they build it themselves. They rip Claude Code or Cursor, pull straight from company data, and ship a working tool in an afternoon. No permissions. No audit trail. No one watching where the data goes.

Security is assumed to be fine because the tool is "just internal."

it's not…

**The solution**

People aren't going to stop building with AI. So we built them a place where it's safe.

With Prized, anyone can spin up a sandbox that comes with company data already attached, scoped to what they should see, with an audit trail on every access. 

From there it's whatever building style they like: describe the tool in our app builder and watch it take shape, or bring a coding agent like Claude Code and build it themselves. Shipping is one click, and the finished tool sits behind your company's sign-in.

The person who runs the workflow finally gets to build the tool for it. Safely, this time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105647&key=user_uploads/2485896/e426b427-8a79-4ca5-b462-b26b98db43e0)

**Secure by default**

Security is enforced in the infrastructure, not left to the person building the tool:

* **Least privilege per tool.** Every tool gets its own database role and integration scopes; it can read and write only what it was granted.
* **Credentials stay out of reach.** Secrets live in a broker and never touch the tool's code or the agent's context, so they can't leak or cross workspace boundaries.
* **Outbound traffic proxy.** External calls only go to explicitly allowed hosts, and integrations are read-only until someone turns writes on.
* **Admin visibility.** IT sees every tool in the org: who built it, what data it reads or writes, who can use it, and risky changes (like a destructive migration) need explicit approval before they ship.

**Your agent, our sandbox**

Already have a favorite coding agent? Bring it. It plugs into the same governed sandbox and ships the same way.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105647&key=user_uploads/2485896/fcfa68c5-8c9f-4d13-b37c-d526e733539a)

**The team**

We worked together at Gander (F24) building fleet management software for private jets. After the company's acquisition by Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR), Marinos continued school at Stanford, and Hudson went on to be an engineer at Suno.

**Our ask**

If any of these describe you, we'd love to talk:

* You work in ops, support, finance, or RevOps and keep waiting on engineering for small tools.
* You lead engineering and one-off tool requests keep eating your roadmap.
* You're in security or IT, wondering where AI-built tools are showing up at your company.

Check us out at[ https://prized.dev/](https://prized.dev/), or reach out at [founders@prized.dev](mailto:founders@prized.dev).

launches.tagline: Every speech model, benchmarked language by language, wired into one API.
launches.body:
Speko is a router for voice models. One API key, and your agent runs on the speech-to-text, LLM and text-to-speech models we measured as best for your language and use case.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108267&key=user_uploads/451241/2038963f-c769-47a9-8fd9-c59f3966027b)

### I picked voice stacks by trial and error for four years

A voice agent is three models in a row: speech-to-text, then an LLM, then text-to-speech. Three vendors, a dozen credible options each. You run a bake-off, you argue about whose numbers are real, and you ship the combination that felt best that month.

Then next week another model drops. And another. Nobody has time to re-run the bake-off, so the stack you picked under deadline quietly becomes the stack you are stuck with for a year.

That is how most voice agents are running today. Not on the best models. On the models that were best whenever someone last had a free week.

Public leaderboards do not settle it either. They are averages over somebody else's audio, in somebody else's conditions.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AjC8WVA96kUBdD09RJMUgFfvxGfxPvL-/](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AjC8WVA96kUBdD09RJMUgFfvxGfxPvL-/view?usp=sharing)

### We measure, then we route

We benchmark the speech models people actually ship on, language by language, and publish everything at [benchmarks.speko.ai](http://benchmarks.speko.ai): word error rate, finalize latency, time to first token, cost per minute. When a vendor ships a new model we test it the same day and the board updates.

Point your agent at Speko and that measurement becomes routing. One API key across every provider we support. Tell us the language and the conditions, and your traffic runs on the stack our numbers say wins. When the numbers change, the routing changes and you rewrite nothing.

If a provider fails when we open the connection, the router drops to the next ranked model on its own.

### Or build the agent with us

You do not need an existing agent to start. A few lines gets a working voice agent live on Speko, and it inherits the same routing from day one.

If you are picking a voice stack right now, start with the numbers at [benchmarks.speko.ai](http://benchmarks.speko.ai), then build on them at [speko.ai](http://speko.ai).

name: Riften
long_description:
Intelligence will be the most valuable asset a company owns. Today, almost every company rents it.

Companies pay a handful of labs one token at a time. Each dollar buys an answer, not an asset. They spend more, but own nothing more.

Riften reverses that.

Change one environment variable and Riften becomes the gateway for a company's AI traffic. We route each request to the lowest-cost model that can do the job, serving most work on open-weight models we host. Customers save money immediately without rebuilding their products.

The gateway is the entry point. Over time, Riften turns the company's work into private models built on open weights and shaped around the business. What begins as cheaper inference becomes an intelligence stack the company owns, runs on infrastructure it controls, and uses to power its most important applications.

We call this earned intelligence. It is created by the company's own work, controlled by the company, and accumulated over time.

The next generation of companies will not rent their intelligence. They will earn it, own it, and compound it. Riften is how they get there.
